messages.content:
Answer submitted by the executor: Acetic acid will have the shortest retention time in RP-HPLC at pH 7. This is because at pH 7, acetic acid (pKa ~4.76) will be predominantly in its deprotonated form (acetate ion), making it negatively charged and highly polar. In reversed-phase HPLC, where the stationary phase is non-polar, polar compounds like the acetate ion interact less with the stationary phase and more with the polar mobile phase, causing them to elute faster. Triethylamine would be partially protonated at pH 7 but still less polar than acetate, while toluene is completely non-polar and would have the strongest retention on the column..
